answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the summit bond on all of them and exposing each to the lotus slash. Because the comet audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 12 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Honest users pay that once, farms 12 times. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
